item.text: Direct web access is working. I found several usable, precisely locatable additions: a July 2000 campaign-finance disclosure signing (4B/7B), an October 2000 civil-rights enforcement proposal (4B), CDC’s 2000 child-wellbeing tables (6B), December 2000 housing and Medicaid/working-family actions (6B), and a contemporaneous congressional record documenting disputed White House gift-reporting allegations (7B, clearly marked as allegation/testimony rather than adjudicated fact). I’m now checking the strongest candidates and boundary limits before composing the handoff.

Targeted continuation completed for 4B, 6B, and 7B. No scoring was performed.

The repository shell remained unavailable because of `bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR`; therefore I could not safely read or update `research-ledger-manifest.json`. I provide the exact manifest delta below for persistence.

### New evidence units

- **CL2000R2-01 — Federal civil-rights enforcement proposal**  
  Clinton’s January 2000 State of the Union proposed $698 million for civil-rights enforcement, including DOJ hate-crime/police-misconduct investigations, EEOC backlog reduction, fair-housing enforcement, and redistricting review. This is direct Clinton policy evidence, but a proposal rather than completed implementation.  
  Source: [2000 State of the Union, civil-rights section](https://clintonwhitehouse4.archives.gov/WH/EOP/nec/html/2000SotuBookFinal.html#civilrights)  
  Period fit: 2000. Attribution: direct presidential proposal. Contrary evidence: proposed funding and legislation do not establish enacted results. Lenses: 4B.3, 4B.6, 4B.7.

- **CL2000R2-02 — Campaign-finance disclosure law signed**  
  On July 1, 2000, Clinton signed Public Law 106-230 requiring 527 organizations to disclose political activities.  
  Source: [GovInfo, Public Papers, pp. 1375–1376](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/PPP-2000-book2/PPP-2000-book2-doc-pg1375/context)  
  Period fit: exact target date. Attribution: direct presidential signature. Contrary evidence: the measure addressed disclosure but did not resolve broader campaign-finance concerns. Lenses: 4B.2, 4B.6, 7B.8.

- **CL2000R2-03 — November 2000 public defense of electoral choice and voter authority**  
  In his November 4 radio address, Clinton explicitly described the upcoming vote as constitutionally guaranteed and stated that voters were the ultimate decision-makers. This is rhetoric, not evidence of election administration.  
  Source: [White House radio address, Nov. 4, 2000](https://clintonwhitehouse4.archives.gov/WH/html/Saturday_November_4_2000.html#)  
  Period fit: exact target date. Attribution: direct speech. Contrary evidence: campaign advocacy and criticism of Congress appear in the same address. Lenses: 4B.1, 4B.3.

- **CL2000R2-04 — 2000 child-wellbeing mortality indicators**  
  The federal *America’s Children 2000* report records preliminary 1998 infant mortality of 7.2 deaths per 1,000 births, child mortality of 34 per 100,000 ages 1–4, and persistent racial disparities, including 1997 Black non-Hispanic infant mortality of 13.7 versus 6.0 for White non-Hispanic infants.  
  Source: [CDC/NCHS report, pp. 6, 41–42, Tables HEALTH5–6](https://stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/47246/cdc_47246_DS1.pdf)  
  Period fit: report published July 2000, indicators lagged to 1997–1998. Attribution: country-level outcome; no direct Clinton causation. Contrary evidence: substantial racial disparities remain. Lenses: 6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.8, 6B.10.

- **CL2000R2-05 — Childhood immunization progress remained incomplete**  
  CDC’s Healthy People 2000 review reports combined coverage of four DTP, three polio, and one MMR doses at 81% in 1998, below the 90% target; individual vaccine coverage varied by vaccine and state.  
  Source: [CDC Healthy People 2000 immunization review](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/healthy_people/hp2000/reviews/immunization.htm#)  
  Period fit: contemporaneous review available in the target period, with 1998 outcome data. Attribution: outcome context, not personal Clinton attribution. Contrary evidence: progress exceeded the 90% target for some vaccines, including Hib. Lenses: 6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.5, 6B.10.

- **CL2000R2-06 — December 2000 housing and homelessness implementation**  
  Clinton announced more than $1 billion in HUD grants for over 200,000 homeless people, including $895 million in Continuum of Care grants and $150 million in emergency shelter grants; the announcement also described a final rule requiring public-housing authorities to promote economic integration.  
  Source: [White House radio address, Dec. 23, 2000](https://clintonwhitehouse4.archives.gov/library/hot_releases/DECEMBER_23_2000.html)  
  Period fit: exact target date. Attribution: direct presidential announcement; implementation assigned to HUD and local authorities. Contrary evidence: announced grants and rules do not prove realized housing outcomes within 2000. Lenses: 6B.1, 6B.2, 6B.3, 8B.2, 8B.6.

- **CL2000R2-07 — Medicaid continuity for welfare-to-work transitions**  
  The December 2000 budget agreement extended Medicaid coverage for one year for people leaving welfare for work, alongside education, health, and labor funding.  
  Source: [White House radio address, Dec. 15, 2000](https://clintonwhitehouse4.archives.gov/library/hot_releases/Mon_18_Dec_2000_115526_-0500.html)  
  Period fit: exact target period. Attribution: Clinton administration negotiated and publicized the agreement; Congress shared responsibility. Contrary evidence: extension was temporary and does not establish long-term coverage. Lenses: 6B.2, 6B.3, 8B.2, 8B.7.

- **CL2000R2-08 — 2000 welfare implementation report**  
  The August 22 White House fact sheet states that all states subject to welfare-reform work requirements met the 1999 requirements, with a 38% national participation rate, and cites CEA’s estimate that welfare reform accounted for approximately one-third of caseload reduction from 1996–1998.  
  Source: [White House welfare reform fact sheet](https://clintonwhitehouse4.archives.gov/textonly/library/hot_releases/Tue_Aug_22_130703_2000.html)  
  Period fit: August 2000 report, using prior-year administrative data. Attribution: administration report and Clinton policy ownership; CEA causal estimate is not personal proof. Contrary evidence: the figures concern caseload and work participation, not poverty depth or job quality. Lenses: 6B.1, 6B.3, 6B.5, 6B.7, 8B.6, 8B.7.

- **CL2000R2-09 — Campaign-finance/personal-interest record remains unresolved**  
  A later FEC legal record describes 2000 fundraising involving Denise Rich, Peter Paul, and Hillary Clinton’s Senate campaign, but it is an allegation-rich complaint record and does not establish Bill Clinton’s personal financial benefit or direction.  
  Source: [FEC MUR 5225 record](https://www.fec.gov/files/legal/murs/5225/00004DFA.pdf), pp. 1–3.  
  Period fit: activities occurred in 1999–2000; record is later and retrospective. Attribution: bounded; documents alleged fundraising relationships, not adjudicated Clinton conduct. Contrary evidence: the record itself is advocacy/complaint material rather than a final factual finding. Lenses: 7B.3, 7B.4, 7B.9. Disposition: `context`, not final evidence.
